instructor: The course structure was not good. There was a very intensive and difficult program. It was not clear what we were going to do, it changed during the process. There was not enough explanation. This course was taught by 3 instructors together and I think dividing it section by section would solve all the problems. In addition to not being able to do this, they also tried to look at too many students in too little time, so both they and the students had a hard time and there were inequalities. The biggest problem was that there was no effort to teach anything in the course. It is logically wrong for people who will be designers to expect development in short feedback periods. The feedback could not be about my shortcomings in terms of design because I could only get feedback on what I did. If I cannot research, learn and apply everything myself and also learn the things I need to develop, I can do this without taking classes anyway. I take classes to learn something, I can already produce something well or badly. I could neither show any development nor did I learn anything. Having a good group of designers does not mean they are good instructors. I think they need to improve some things.  If you encounter projects that are given low grades, you have to correct this and think that the problem is not only with the student but also with you. When there was a problem with the functioning of the course, it was expected from the student to fix it. When there was noise, a problem in the queue, or someone distracted the instructors, they expected intervention from the students. Although there were many people around the instructor who were distracting, openly disrespectful or trespassing, no intervention was made. We could not get feedback on where the final projects were lacking or needed to be improved.On top of that, I think some students were discriminated against. Such as not deducting grades from people I knew were uploading late, and giving longer feedback to some.
course: I think the project durations in the course are not appropriate. While very long time is given for projects that could be completed in a shorter time if the process was smooth, the final project was given a very short time despite being intense compared to the others. I think the project contents should change in a course that I know had 3 projects before. In my second year, we were doing projects about the content determined by lottery in the studio course. This shortened the thinking part of the project. We were still doing research, but it was not so clear what we wanted to do. If the aim is to develop our creative side, maybe it is better not to have a lottery, but in real life, we design about the works given to us, in fact, the moments when we produce something from scratch can be very limited. I also think that it was made difficult while it could have been easy to solve the time and order issue in the studio. On the positive side, I found the first project to be developing. The second project was a project where very little was expected for its duration. Although it was a good choice to focus on using AI, I think there should have been a separate course for this. Using it as a tool in the course was like a necessity after a certain point.Also, poster design is a part of our job, yes, but it is better to be given a short time as a project and learn something with different content. For example, I thought that the second poster project would involve other things like advertising design, a short video commercial shoot, etc. While I thought that I would learn packaging in the third project, I was asked to make a comic book that would be more suitable for fine arts students and packaging was requested recently, so we did something on our own without getting enough feedback and making any progress.
assistant: There was an assistant or part-time instructor named İrem (I don't know its exact name because I've seen it so rarely and for such a short time) who came and helped me with feedback on my final project, which I thought was very good. There was also someone at the beginning of the semester, but I didn't see her having much of an impact.
